codes.name: Tool execution
codes.summary: The harness gives the model callable tools, runs each call and returns the result within the turn.

codes.name: MCP connection
codes.summary: Connect to an MCP server (local stdio or remote HTTP), discover its tools and route calls to it; equivalent connector mechanisms count.

codes.name: Read supplied files
codes.summary: Read files the user supplies (pdf, docx, xlsx, eml, text, images) whole.

codes.name: Hand back files
codes.summary: Write a file and hand it to the user.

codes.name: Real filesystem
codes.summary: User-named paths, recursive folder walks, run and sibling output folders, stable paths.

codes.name: Storage that outlives the session
codes.summary: A file written in one session can be found in a later one without being attached again.

codes.name: Run bundled scripts
codes.summary: Run the skills' bundled Python scripts; P1's facts are judged against each skill's exact needs.

codes.name: External executables
codes.summary: Poppler, LibreOffice, tesseract, headless Chromium, an SVG rasteriser or the codex CLI on the path.

codes.name: Fetch a URL
codes.summary: Fetch a public page and quote it; skills that hash what they fetch add the raw-bytes probe.

codes.name: Web search
codes.summary: Search the web and return an address the user can check.

codes.name: See rendered pages
codes.summary: The model looks at a rendered page image and reports what is on it.

codes.name: Word OOXML structure
codes.summary: Read tracked changes, comments and tables in a Word file, not just its text.

codes.name: Isolated workers
codes.summary: A fresh-context worker that sees only its packet, with the model chosen per worker.

codes.name: Conversation transcripts
codes.summary: Quote the current session's own words and events, and say which are read and which reconstructed.

codes.name: Background or scheduled runs
codes.summary: A run that happens after the turn ends and can read and write files.

codes.name: Interactive HTML round trip
codes.summary: The user opens a generated offline HTML page, and the file it downloads comes back to the skill.

codes.name: File digest by the host
codes.summary: Compute a SHA-256 of a file where no bundled script does it for the skill.

codes.name: Skill folder on disk
codes.summary: The skill's scripts, assets and sibling skills are reachable by path.

codes.name: Call a skill by name
codes.summary: An explicit-invocation-only skill does not fire on its own, but fires when the user calls it by name.

probes.title: Does a bundled script actually run, and in what?
probes.settles: Whether a script packaged inside a skill is executed at all, and what interpreter and libraries it would run under. Nothing ships with a script under the no-scripts policy, so a result changes no tier; it is the input to the maintainer's decision about that policy and to the original, not re-scoped, paths of closing-bible, definition-check and read-redline.

harness.steps: Run `python3 <skill>/scripts/hprobe.py env --run <run>`. It records the Python version, the importable packages (pypdf, pdfplumber, docx, openpyxl, PIL, fitz, playwright), every executable the vendored skills call (pdftoppm, pdfinfo, pdftotext, soffice, tesseract, chromium, rsvg-convert, magick, inkscape, codex) and whether the script could read a fixture and write to the output folder. Show the printed line verbatim. If the command cannot be run, record P1 as fail with observer agent and say why.

cowork.setup: Cannot be run from the released bundles, because no shipped skill contains a script. Needs a throwaway single-skill probe package containing scripts/probe.py, which prints one line naming sys.version, platform.platform(), whether pypdf, pdfplumber, docx, openpyxl, PIL, fitz and playwright import, and whether pdftoppm, pdfinfo, pdftotext, soffice, tesseract, chromium, rsvg-convert, magick, inkscape and codex are on the path; it also reads one attached file and writes one file to the Output folder. The SKILL.md says to run it and report its output verbatim. The harness-probe skill's `hprobe.py env` is that script.
cowork.prompt: Run the environment probe and show me its output exactly as printed.
cowork.pass: The reply contains the fingerprint line with a real Python version string of 3.12 or later, the package and executable lists, and a confirmed read of the attached file and write to the Output folder.
cowork.fail: A reply that paraphrases the script, describes what it would print, or reports the script's contents as instructions.

probes.title: Does a file written in one session come back in the next?
probes.settles: Whether state written to the Cowork folder is reachable from a later session without the lawyer attaching it. No tier turns on it, by design: every cross-session design brings its own state instead. It is an ergonomics upgrade for sigpack's ledger, regulatory's refresh baseline, legalquants step 3b, lq-reflect step 8b and lq-apply step 2b.

harness.steps: Session one: run `hprobe.py check P2 --run <run> --phase write`, then use your own file tool to write the printed token into `lq-probe-persist.txt` in the user's workspace root (not the run folder). Tell the user to come back in a new session on a later day. Session two, with nothing attached: find `lq-probe-persist.txt` yourself, then run `hprobe.py check P2 --run <run> --phase read --answer <token you found>`. If the run folder itself is gone, record P2 as fail.

cowork.setup: None beyond two sessions on different days.
cowork.prompt:
Session 1: Create a file called probe-ledger.json in my Cowork Output folder containing exactly {"probe":"lqc","n":1} and tell me where you put it.
A new session on a later day, with nothing attached: Open probe-ledger.json from my Cowork folder, tell me what n is, then save it back with n increased by one.
cowork.pass: It finds the file without the tester attaching it, reports n as 1, writes 2 — and a third session reads 2.
cowork.fail: It cannot find the file, or asks the tester to attach it.

probes.title: Does Cowork report tracked changes in a Word document?
probes.settles: Whether Cowork can see tracked insertions, deletions and comments in a Word document at all, and whether it returns an honest nil on a clean copy. Word tracked changes are nowhere mentioned in Microsoft's pages.

harness.steps: Open `<run>/fixtures/docx/tracked.docx` and `clean.docx` with your own tools. For tracked.docx list the inserted text and its author, the deleted text and its author, and the comment text. Then run `hprobe.py check P3 --run <run> --answer "ins=<text>;ins_author=<name>; del=<text>;del_author=<name>;comment=<text>;clean=none"` (clean=none if clean.docx has no tracked changes, otherwise list what you saw).

cowork.setup: A two-page synthetic DOCX with tracked insertions and deletions by two named authors and one comment; plus a clean copy of the same file with the changes accepted.
cowork.prompt: List every tracked change in this agreement: the exact inserted and deleted text, who made it, and where it sits. Tell me if there are none.
cowork.pass: Insertions and deletions listed separately with authors, and the comment noted; and, on the clean copy, it says there are none rather than inventing some.
cowork.fail: It reads the document as though the changes had been accepted and reports no changes.

probes.title: Can Cowork tell what is on a page?
probes.settles: Whether Cowork can say, page by page, what a PDF carries — strikethrough and underline, handwriting and signatures, and whether a page is scanned rather than typed. OCR, scanned PDFs and handwriting are nowhere mentioned.

harness.steps: Look at `<run>/fixtures/vision/page.png` as an image (not via OCR text). It shows a short code in large letters and a scribbled mark in one corner. Run `hprobe.py check P4 --run <run> --answer "code=<code>;corner=<top-left|top-right|bottom-left|bottom-right>"`.

cowork.setup: A four-page synthetic PDF: page 2 carries redline markup (strikethrough and underline), page 3 is a scanned image of a signature block signed over a printed name, page 4 is clean.
cowork.prompt: Go through this PDF page by page. For each page tell me whether anything is struck through or underlined, whether there is handwriting or a signature, and whether the page is scanned rather than typed.
cowork.pass: Correct per-page answers, including that page 3 is an image and is signed, without being told.
cowork.fail: It describes pages it cannot see, or reports the scanned page as blank or as text.

probes.title: What does a resumed task remember?
probes.settles: What re-enters the model's context when a task is resumed, and whether a brand-new task can see the previous one. The mechanism of continuation is documented; what it carries is not. No tier turns on it: it bounds lq-reflect's week-wide alternative.

harness.steps: Session one: remember the token printed by `hprobe.py check P5 --run <run> --phase token` and stop. Next day, resume that same task or conversation and ask what the token was; then open a brand-new task and ask the same. Record P5 pass if the resumed task has it and the new one does not, with `hprobe.py record P5 pass --observer user`.

cowork.setup: Two sessions plus one resumption, over two days.
cowork.prompt:
Session 1: Remember this reference for later: ALDERNEY-7. Draft me two lines about anything.
Resuming that task from the task list the next day: What was the reference I gave you?
Then, in a brand-new task: What did I ask you in my previous Cowork task?
cowork.pass: The resumed task returns ALDERNEY-7 unprompted; the new task does not know.
cowork.fail: The resumed task does not have it, or — the bigger finding — the new task does.

probes.title: Is web search on in this tenant, and what comes back?
probes.settles: Whether web search is enabled here, and whether what comes back is a page address the lawyer can check or a rendering they cannot. It confirms a limit rather than lifting one, and informs lq-ask's optional step and regulatory's locator-only use of search.

harness.steps: Search the web (not from memory) for section 1 of the Bribery Act 2010 on legislation.gov.uk. Run `hprobe.py check P6 --run <run> --url <the address you read> --answer "<the opening sentence, word for word>" --bytes <length of the page you fetched, or 0 if your tool only gave you a rendering>`.

cowork.prompt: Search the web and quote me, word for word, the opening sentence of the official text you find at legislation.gov.uk for the Bribery Act 2010 section 1, and give me the address of the page you read.
cowork.pass: A URL and a quotation, the byte length of the page as fetched (or a plain statement that only a rendering came back), plus whatever the client says about web search.
cowork.fail: A refusal naming a disabled web-search setting — which is an equally useful result and should be reported with the tenant's admin posture if known.

probes.title: Can a skill's output carry a file that shipped with the skill?
probes.settles: Whether a companion file packaged inside a skill reaches something the lawyer receives. Carrying the asset is documented; reaching an output is not. Two arms, one probe: P7a a text or HTML template, P7b a bundled binary image. P7a is free today and should be the first probe the programme runs.

harness.steps: Copy `/assets/fixtures/badge.png` into `/outputs/` and write `/outputs/card.html` that shows it with an tag. Then run `hprobe.py check P7 --run `. The badge must be the packaged file, byte for byte, not a new image.

cowork.setup: P7a: none; run it against the shipped legaldesign skill, which carries HTML templates as companions. P7b: package a probe skill carrying a small PNG and an HTML template that references it.
cowork.prompt:
P7a: Turn the attached advice note into a one-pager using your supplied template, and tell me which of your template files you used.
P7b: Build the card from your supplied template and tell me which of your packaged files it used.
cowork.pass: P7a: the produced HTML visibly uses the packaged template's structure and the reply names the companion file. P7b: the rendered page shows the image and the reply names the file.
cowork.fail: P7a: generic HTML, or a named file that was not used. P7b, recorded separately: the page renders without the image, or the reply claims an image that is not there.

probes.title: Can Cowork build a PDF out of chosen pages of supplied PDFs?
probes.settles: Whether Cowork can assemble a new PDF from chosen pages of supplied ones. Merging or splitting PDFs is nowhere mentioned, and the PDF built-in's entire description is the single line "Work with PDF documents".

harness.steps: Build `<run>/outputs/assembled.pdf` containing page 3 of `<run>/fixtures/pdf/first.pdf` followed by pages 1 and 2 of `<run>/fixtures/pdf/second.pdf`, using your own tools. Then run `hprobe.py check P8 --run <run>`.

cowork.setup: Two synthetic four-page PDFs with distinguishable page content.
cowork.prompt: Make me one new PDF containing page 3 of the first document and pages 1 and 2 of the second, in that order, and tell me how many pages it has.
cowork.pass: A downloadable PDF in the Output folder with exactly those three pages in that order and their content intact.
cowork.fail: A reply that describes the pages instead of producing the file, or a PDF with the wrong pages or order.

probes.title: Does an Excel workbook survive a round trip with its arithmetic intact?
probes.settles: Whether a workbook's structure and formulas survive being handed back and forth. The round trip itself is documented; whether the arithmetic survives is not. After P3, the probe with the widest reach in the document-pipeline half.

harness.steps: Open `<run>/fixtures/xlsx/tracker.xlsx`. Add the four rows listed in `<run>/fixtures/xlsx/new-rows.txt` below the existing six, keep the count row's formula a live formula, and save the result as `<run>/outputs/tracker-out.xlsx`. Then run `hprobe.py check P9 --run <run>`.

cowork.setup: None; two sessions.
cowork.prompt:
Session 1: Build me a tracker workbook with columns Document, Issue, Status, Quote, Locator and these six rows, and add a row at the bottom that counts how many rows are filled.
A fresh session with the returned workbook attached: Add these four documents as new rows, fill the Status column for them, and give the workbook back to me unchanged apart from the new rows.
cowork.pass: The returned file keeps the original six rows, the column order, the count formula as a formula, and its recalculated value.
cowork.fail: Rows dropped or reordered, columns renamed, or the count arriving as a hard-coded number rather than a live formula.

probes.title: Can Cowork produce a Word document carrying real tracked changes?
probes.settles: Whether Cowork can write a Word file whose edits are recorded as tracked changes rather than applied as plain text. Producing a Word document with tracked changes or comments is nowhere stated. Neither dependent step is load-bearing; both improve.

harness.steps: Open `<run>/fixtures/docx/clause.docx` and apply the three edits in `<run>/fixtures/docx/edits.txt` as Word tracked changes attributed to "Review", not as plain edits. Save as `<run>/outputs/clause-tracked.docx` and run `hprobe.py check P10 --run <run>`.

cowork.setup: A short supplied agreement clause.
cowork.prompt: Give me back this clause as a Word document with my three edits recorded as tracked changes attributed to "Review", not as plain edited text.
cowork.pass: Opening the file in Word shows insertions and deletions in the review pane.
cowork.fail: A document with the edits applied as plain text, or coloured text that is not a tracked change.

probes.title: What can a skill see and quote of its own session?
probes.settles: Whether a skill can quote the lawyer's own words back verbatim, list the files created and list the skills and tools used, and whether it says honestly which of those it is reading and which it is reconstructing. A refusal blocks nothing: it forces every quote to come from an attached file.

harness.steps: Ask the user to type a sentence of their own choosing at the start of the session (before the probes). Near the end, quote it back word for word, list the files created in this session and the tools and skills used, and say for each whether you are reading it or reconstructing it. The user judges and you record with `hprobe.py record P11 <pass|fail| fluent-fake> --observer user`.

cowork.setup: In one conversation, do some work first: type a distinctive sentence, have a file created, invoke a second skill.
cowork.prompt: Quote back, word for word, the sentence I typed at the start of this session; list the files created in this session; and list the skills and tools used. Say for each whether you are reading it or reconstructing it.
cowork.pass: A verbatim quote, the correct file list, the correct skill and tool list, each with honest attribution.
cowork.fail: Two distinguishable ways: a refusal (usable — the cards adapt around it) or a fluent paraphrase presented as a quote.

probes.title: Browser use: does what it reads reach the skill?
probes.settles: Two things. (a) Availability: is browser use enabled in this tenant, and what did it take to enable it — it needs Edge, runs only in Cowork on the web, and is disabled by default until an admin turns it on. (b) Quotability: does page content or a downloaded file become something the session, and therefore a skill, can quote. No design depends on it.

harness.steps: Fetch https://example.com/ with your own tool (a fetch or browser tool, not search) and run `hprobe.py check P12 --run <run> --answer "<the page's first heading, verbatim>" --bytes <byte length if your tool reports it, else 0>`.

cowork.setup: Cowork on the web in Microsoft Edge, on a device where Edge is installed, in a tenant where an admin has performed the enable steps. Record what the posture was before the tester asked, who had to act, and the tenant's DLP and site-blocking posture. A tenant where the admin declines is a reportable result, not a failed run.
cowork.prompt: Open the page at <public URL> and quote its first heading and the first sentence under it. Tell me how you retrieved it, how many bytes the page was as you received it (or that you only received a rendering), and whether that page is now one of my session files.
cowork.pass: The quote comes back, Cowork names the route, and it states plainly whether the content is now a session file.
cowork.fail: The content comes back as a summary rather than quotable text; or a refusal citing a blocked site (still a useful result — record it with the posture).

probes.title: Can a scheduled run work over files placed earlier?
probes.settles: Whether an automated run can read files the lawyer placed earlier, write outputs, and load a custom skill. The scheduling machinery is documented; what a run can reach is not. No card is built on it; any of them may offer a cadence as a closing line, and must name the twenty-five scheduled-prompt cap when they do.

harness.steps: Run `hprobe.py check P13 --run <run> --phase arm` and note the command it prints. Use the harness's own scheduler to run that command at least ten minutes from now, after this turn has ended. In a later session run `hprobe.py check P13 --run <run> --phase verify`. Record whether it was a scheduled prompt or a process that outlived the turn in --notes.

cowork.setup: A file already sitting in the Cowork folder, and a custom skill installed.
cowork.prompt: Every Monday at 9am, use the <name> skill on closing-register.xlsx in my Cowork folder and save the updated register back.
cowork.pass: The Runs tab shows it ran; an output file appears; the output reflects the placed file; and the run history shows the custom skill was loaded. Record whether the run was a scheduled prompt or a process that outlived the turn.
cowork.fail: The schedule exists but the skill is not invoked, or nothing is written, or the run reports success with no output.

probes.title: Enterprise Search as a people finder
probes.settles: Whether Enterprise Search can answer who in the organisation has worked on a topic, with a quotable document behind each name. Microsoft's whole statement about it is the line "Enterprise Search Search across your organization".

harness.steps: Cowork only: run the Cowork prompt above in a tenant with real internal material and record the outcome with `hprobe.py record P14 <outcome> --observer user`. On any other harness, record P14 as not-run.

cowork.setup: A tenant with real internal material behind the chosen topic.
cowork.prompt: Who in my organisation has worked on <a topic with real internal material behind it>? Name up to three people and, for each, quote the document that shows it.
cowork.pass: Named people, each with a quotable document.
cowork.fail: Documents with no people attached, or names with nothing behind them.

probes.title: Can the harness connect to an MCP server and call one of its tools?
probes.settles: Whether the harness can reach an MCP server at all - start or connect to it, list its tools and route a call to it - which is how lq-mcp, CourtListener and the C5 integrations of definition-check and conform would arrive. No skill requires MCP, but fifteen use it if present.

harness.steps: Register the bundled server with the harness (see references/mcp-setup.md; for example `claude mcp add hprobe -- python3 <skill>/scripts/mcp_probe_server.py --run <run>`). Run `hprobe.py check P15 --run <run> --phase nonce` for a nonce, call the server's `probe_challenge` tool with it, and run `hprobe.py check P15 --run <run> --answer <digest>`. If only some other MCP server is connected, call one of its read-only tools, quote the result, and record P15 with `hprobe.py record P15 pass --observer user` once the user confirms it.

cowork.setup: A connected MCP server. The harness-probe skill ships one: `harness-probe/scripts/mcp_probe_server.py`, a standard-library stdio server whose `probe_challenge` tool answers a nonce with a keyed digest only the server can compute. In Cowork, a declarative agent connector pointing at any remote MCP server the tenant has approved.
cowork.prompt: List the tools the connected probe server offers, call probe_challenge with the nonce 7Q4-ALDER, and give me exactly what it returned.
cowork.pass: The digest the server logged for that nonce comes back verbatim, and the server is named.
cowork.fail: A digest the server never issued, a description of what the tool would return, or a reply that the server is not reachable.

probes.title: Can the agent walk a folder it was pointed at, and make one beside it?
probes.settles: Whether the harness can list a user-named folder recursively with exact relative paths and an exact count, and create a sibling run folder - the filesystem fifteen upstream skills require for a data room, a production, a closing folder or a matter folder.

harness.steps: With your own file tools (not hprobe.py), list every file under `<run>/fixtures/tree/` by its path relative to that folder, one per line, and save the list as `<run>/outputs/sibling-run/listing.txt`, creating the sibling-run folder. Then run `hprobe.py check P16 --run <run> --count <how many files you found>`.

cowork.setup: A folder of 23 synthetic files in nested subfolders (the skill generates it).
cowork.prompt: List every file under the attached folder by its path relative to the folder, tell me how many there are, then create a folder called run beside it and save the list there as listing.txt.
cowork.pass: Every relative path, the exact count, and listing.txt in a new sibling folder.
cowork.fail: A partial list, a count that does not match the list, or paths invented from the folder's apparent naming pattern.

probes.title: Can the harness compute a file's SHA-256?
probes.settles: Whether the host can fingerprint a file when no bundled script does it. organize-case-docs requires it for its manifest, and every fallback receipt in the review skills depends on it.

harness.steps: Compute the SHA-256 of `<run>/fixtures/hash/blob.bin` with your own tool (a shell, a code tool, or a hash tool - not hprobe.py), then run `hprobe.py check P17 --run <run> --answer <hex digest>`.

cowork.setup: Any small binary file; the skill generates one with random bytes.
cowork.prompt: Give me the SHA-256 of the attached file, in hex, and say how you computed it.
cowork.pass: The digest matches one computed independently.
cowork.fail: A digest that does not match, or a plausible-looking hex string with no computation behind it.

probes.title: Can the harness fetch a URL's raw bytes into a file?
probes.settles: Whether a fetch returns the bytes a publisher served, saved where they can be hashed, rather than a rendering. regulatory's verified route rests on it; a model's summary of a page is not the page.

harness.steps: Download https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LegalQuants/lq-plugin-oss/fa5a6681dc3cc9a08fa9ed48a5fd213057edafa0/LICENSE byte for byte to `<run>/outputs/fetched-LICENSE` with your own tool, then run `hprobe.py check P18 --run <run>`.

cowork.prompt: Download https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LegalQuants/lq-plugin-oss/fa5a6681dc3cc9a08fa9ed48a5fd213057edafa0/LICENSE byte for byte into my Output folder and tell me its size in bytes and its SHA-256.
cowork.pass: The saved file's size and SHA-256 match the published file.
cowork.fail: A file whose bytes differ (re-encoded, reformatted, summarised), or a size and digest with no file behind them.

probes.title: Can the harness run an isolated worker that sees only its packet?
probes.settles: Whether the harness can hand a sealed packet to a fresh-context worker (a subagent or a separate model call) that cannot see the parent's context, and say which model ran it. Nine upstream skills fan out work this way, and docreview and diligence also need the model chosen per worker.

harness.steps: Run `hprobe.py check P19 --run <run> --phase canary` and keep the printed canary in this conversation only. Start a fresh worker (subagent or separate model call) whose whole input is the contents of `<run>/fixtures/sub/packet.txt`. Save the worker's reply verbatim to `<run>/outputs/worker-reply.txt`, then run `hprobe.py check P19 --run <run> --model "<model the worker ran on>"`.

cowork.setup: A packet file holding one instruction and a token, and a canary phrase that only the parent conversation holds (the skill generates both).
cowork.prompt: Remember the phrase SILVER-HERON. Now give the attached packet to a separate worker with none of this conversation, and show me its reply and which model ran it.
cowork.pass: The worker does what the packet says, does not know the canary, and the model is named.
cowork.fail: The worker knows the canary (it shared the context), or the parent answers in the worker's name.

probes.title: Can the user open a generated page and hand back the file it saves?
probes.settles: Whether the interactive HTML round trip works: the user opens an offline page the skill generated, makes choices, the page saves them as a JSON download, and that file comes back to the skill. legaldesign, docreview and diligence require it.

harness.steps: Give the user `<run>/outputs/roundtrip.html` (written by init). Ask them to open it in a browser, tick Alpha and Gamma, press Download decisions and hand the downloaded `hprobe-decisions.json` back to you; put it at `<run>/inputs/hprobe-decisions.json`, then run `hprobe.py check P20 --run <run>`.

cowork.setup: A generated roundtrip.html (the skill writes one with a nonce).
cowork.prompt: Open the attached page, tick Alpha and Gamma, press Download decisions, and give the downloaded file back to me.
cowork.pass: The returned JSON carries the page's nonce, Alpha and Gamma ticked, and whether browser storage worked.
cowork.fail: The page will not open, the download never happens, the file cannot be handed back, or the agent describes the choices instead of reading the file.

probes.title: Is the skill folder on disk, with its scripts and assets reachable?
probes.settles: Whether a skill's own folder exists on a real filesystem, so a bundled script can import its sibling modules and read ../assets by relative path - which every scripted upstream skill, and the cross-skill calls of the companion set and conform, assume.

harness.steps: Run `python3 <skill>/scripts/hprobe.py check P21 --run <run>`. It imports its sibling module, reads `<skill>/assets/fixtures/marker.bin` by relative path and lists any sibling skill folders it can see.

cowork.setup: A probe skill whose script imports a sibling module and reads a packaged asset.
cowork.prompt: Run the skill's self-check script and show me its output exactly as printed.
cowork.pass: The script reports its own path, a successful sibling import and the asset's digest.
cowork.fail: The script cannot be found or run, or the output is described rather than printed.

probes.title: Can the harness annotate a PDF with highlights and comment-pane notes?
probes.settles: Whether a PDF can be returned carrying real annotations - a highlight and a note in the comments pane - rather than a description of them. read-redline's annotated copy depends on it.

harness.steps: Add a highlight annotation and a comment (text) annotation whose contents are the token in `<run>/fixtures/pdf/annotate-token.txt` to `<run>/fixtures/pdf/plain.pdf`, with your own tools, and save it as `<run>/outputs/annotated.pdf`. Then run `hprobe.py check P22 --run <run>`.

cowork.setup: A one-page synthetic PDF with a known sentence.
cowork.prompt: Highlight the sentence that starts "The Purchaser shall" in the attached PDF and add a comment on it saying REVIEW-7, and give me the annotated PDF.
cowork.pass: Opening the PDF shows the highlight and the comment in the comments pane.
cowork.fail: A PDF with no annotations, coloured text drawn into the page, or a description of the change.

probes.title: Can the harness fill a packaged Word template and edit its table in place?
probes.settles: Whether a .docx shipped inside a skill can be copied, have one table cell changed in place and come back with its formatting intact - what document-discovery's response shell and closing-checklist's table edit need.

harness.steps: Copy `<skill>/assets/fixtures/template.docx` to `<run>/outputs/template-filled.docx`, change the second data row's Status cell to the token in `<run>/fixtures/docx/status-token.txt` without touching anything else, and run `hprobe.py check P23 --run <run>`.

cowork.setup: A packaged template.docx with a styled three-row table.

probes.title: Does an explicit-invocation-only skill stay quiet until it is called by name?
probes.settles: Whether the harness honours `disable-model-invocation` (or `allow_implicit_invocation: false`): the skill must not fire on a matching prompt, but must fire when the user calls it by name. Nine upstream skills are explicit-only and are unreachable without this.

harness.steps: Ask the user to install `harness-probe-invoke` beside this skill. Ask them to send "Check whether the invoke probe is wired up." and note whether that skill fired; then ask them to call it by name (for example `/harness-probe-invoke`). Run `hprobe.py check P24 --run <run> --answer <token it returned> --implicit <fired|quiet>`.

cowork.setup: The companion skill harness-probe-invoke installed beside harness-probe. It is explicit-only and answers with a fixed token when called.
cowork.prompt: First: "Check whether the invoke probe is wired up." Then, in a new message, call the harness-probe-invoke skill by name.
cowork.pass: The first message does not run the skill; the second does and returns its token.
cowork.fail: The skill fires on the first message, or cannot be called by name at all.

probes.title: Does a tool call actually execute?
probes.settles: Whether the harness runs the model's tool calls and returns real results, rather than letting a call be narrated. Nineteen upstream skills need tool execution and nine more fall back without it.

harness.steps: Read `<run>/fixtures/tools/token.txt` with a file-reading tool and run `hprobe.py check P25 --run <run> --answer "<exact contents>"`. If you have no tools, say so and record P25 as fail.

cowork.setup: A file whose contents nobody has seen (the skill generates it).
cowork.prompt: Read the attached file with a tool and give me its exact contents.
cowork.pass: The exact contents, which cannot be guessed.
cowork.fail: Contents that do not match, or an account of reading it with nothing read.

probes.title: Can the harness read every supplied format, whole?
probes.settles: Whether a PDF, a Word file, a workbook, an email and a long text file can each be read in full, so a code on the last page is found. IN is required by sixteen upstream skills, and pressuretest and cite-check read documents whole.

harness.steps: Read every file in `<run>/fixtures/in/` (report.pdf, memo.docx, sheet.xlsx, message.eml, long.txt) in full and run `hprobe.py check P26 --run <run> --answer "pdf=<code>;docx=<code>;xlsx=<code>;eml=<code>;txt=<code>"`. On a harness without file tools, ask the user to attach the static copies in `in/` inside `<skill>/assets/fixtures/static.zip` instead.

cowork.setup: Five synthetic files, each with a code buried at the end.
cowork.prompt: Each attached file has a line starting CODE: near its end. Give me the code from every file, naming the file.
cowork.pass: All five codes, each from the right file.
cowork.fail: Any code missing, wrong, or invented; or a long file read only in part.

probes.title: Can the harness hand a file back to the user?
probes.settles: Whether the skill can produce a file the user receives and can open - the most basic output every document skill relies on.

harness.steps: Write the token in `<run>/fixtures/out/token.txt` as the only line of `<run>/outputs/hello-probe.txt` with your own file tool, tell the user where it is, and run `hprobe.py check P27 --run <run>`.
